newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka troops, rebels in renewed fighting in north.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka troops, rebels in renewed fighting in north.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops and Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels have exchanged artillery and mortar fire in renewed fighting in the island's north, military officials said on Saturday.

The clandestine Voice of Tiger radio, monitored in the government-held town of Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, said the army had fired shells at rebel positions late on Friday after troops edged out of northeastern Nedunkeni following a long lull in fighting.
"There was (a) heavy shell attack and six civilians were wounded (on Friday)," the radio said.
A Defence Ministry statement on Saturday confirmed the firing, but gave no details. It only said troops were dominating areas ahead of northern defences.
Residents in Vavuniya said they heard shell fire from the direction of Nedunkeni, which is 40 km (25 miles) northeast of the government-held town, through most of Friday night.
Government troops captured Nedunkeni in the early days of "Operation Jayasikuru", or "Sure of Victory", which was launched in May to open a strategic land route to the northern Jaffna peninsula.
The offensive slowed down after rebels launched two fierce counter-attacks on the military last month. Scores of rebels and soldiers were killed in the attacks.
The lull was broken this week when rebels attacked the army's forward positions near Nedunkeni late on Wednesday. The Defence Ministry said the attack was repulsed.
At least 60 rebels and 17 soldiers were killed in the fighting and several more were wounded, it added.
The Voice of Tiger radio said on Saturday that six guerrillas were killed in shell fire on Thursday.
Separately, military officials in the east said on Saturday the navy had recovered several rebel mines in the outer harbour of the port city of Trincomalee on Friday.
They said the mines were destroyed.

Trincomalee, 260 km (160 miles) east of the capital Colombo, is the biggest base of the Sri Lankan navy and the site of a rebel attack in 1995 that led to the breakdown in peace talks between the government and LTTE.

The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
